A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same PLDM study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original Two-Rooms and Diverse PointMaze experiments, including data-efficiency, trajectory-stitching, chasing, layout-generalization, and timing results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Ant-U-Maze evaluations, controlled ablations, reconstruction-based comparisons, representation analyses, and statistical tests.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 adds predictor ensembles and a discounted ensemble-variance penalty to PLDM planning. Appendix C removes the temporal-variance loss and introduces an Ant-specific architecture combining encoded position with raw proprioception. Appendix J specifies five predictors for Two-Rooms and Ant, and disables the inverse-dynamics loss for Two-Rooms.

E1.justification: v2 adds Ant-U-Maze quadruped navigation with 29-dimensional states and eight-dimensional actions, extending evaluation beyond point-mass navigation to articulated control. The original Two-Rooms, chasing, and Diverse PointMaze scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Appendix F adds two evaluated model-based comparators: adapted DreamerV3 without reward or policy learning, and Reconstruction, which replaces PLDM's VICReg objective with pixel reconstruction. These substantially expand comparison beyond the original model-free baselines. Ant-U-Maze uses the existing six-method comparison set.

E3.justification: New protocols include Ant-U-Maze training on five million noisy expert-policy transitions, trajectory lengths of 25–500, and ten evaluation trials; KL-divergence planning for adapted DreamerV3; and replanning intervals of 1, 4, 16, and 32. Existing PLDM settings also change, including the sequence-length-33 learning rate from 0.0007 to 0.0014.

E4.justification: v2 adds loss-component ablations across Two-Rooms and Diverse PointMaze, uncertainty-penalty ablations, reconstruction-objective comparisons, and HILP representation diagnostics on unseen layouts. The original timing analysis becomes a latency-versus-success study. Ant-U-Maze additionally tests whether trajectory-stitching findings extend to more complex control.

E5.justification: Table 2 and the Two-Rooms curves switch from standard deviations to standard errors. Appendix H introduces pooled Welch tests and explicitly reports additional runs bringing selected comparisons to ten seeds. Main captions still specify three seeds while Appendix H refers to five, leaving the broader run-count provenance unclear.

E6.justification: PLDM's good-quality Two-Rooms result changes from 79.6% to 97.8% in Table 2, and its sample-efficiency curves are substantially revised alongside method and setting changes. New Table 6 reports adapted DreamerV3 at 24.0%, Reconstruction at 26.2%, and PLDM at 97.4%. Ant, ablation, timing, statistical, and representation-analysis findings are also added or revised.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation now defines ensemble-based prediction and goal costs plus a discounted variance penalty, while Appendix C removes the temporal-variance term. These are substantive objective-definition changes; the deterministic MDP assumptions remain unchanged, and neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims: model-free methods suit abundant high-quality data, while PLDM offers robustness, data efficiency, and generalization to new layouts and tasks. Navigation was already the stated experimental scope; the added evidence does not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 removes the explanation that dynamics learning cannot fully exploit high-quality trajectories and instead concludes that all methods perform well. v2 adds interpretations of HILP's representation failure and reconstruction-based planning, and reframes planning cost through a latency–accuracy tradeoff. Limitations now explicitly identify manipulation and partial observability as untested settings.

D1.justification: v2 supplies Ant data-generation instructions, architecture listings, parameter counts, and hyperparameters, plus ensemble and uncertainty-penalty settings. Appendix I newly discloses V100 hardware, experiments taking up to one day, and estimated total research expenditure of 500–2000 GPU days. Existing project and baseline-code access links are retained.

R1.justification: Related work is condensed, removing discussions of works including Frans et al., Chen et al., and Cobbe et al. v2 adds an imitation-learning contrast citing Zare et al. and relates its uncertainty regularizer to expectile-based offline RL. The overarching research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, experimental narrative, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. Sections are retitled, appendix organization changes, and single-maze results move into the environment appendix. These are substantial editorial changes beyond the added scientific material.

P2.justification: The opening overview and maze figures exchange positions; Two-Rooms illustrations and trajectory examples are combined and redrawn; and the chasing display is redesigned with an Ant panel. New Ant, ensemble-ablation, and HILP-distance plots accompany additional ablation and significance tables. The timing table gains replanning and normalized-success columns.

improvement.justification: v1 tested only point-mass navigation and justified reconstruction-free learning mainly through prior literature. v2 adds articulated-control evidence, direct reconstruction comparisons, and controlled loss ablations, substantially strengthening validation of the central approach. Failure diagnostics and latency–accuracy measurements also clarify practical behavior. Ambiguous seed provenance and unexplained PLDM differences between Tables 2 and 6 remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantial evidential gains.
